Title: Sensory evaluation of commercial coffee brands in Colombia
Authors: Edis Mauricio Sanmiguel JaimesRelated, Igor Barahona Torres, Héctor Hugo Pérez-Villarreal
Date: Wed Feb  3 17:19:13 2016

Colombian coffee farmers have traditionally focused their efforts on activities including seeding, planting and drying. Strategic issues to successfully compete in the industry, such as branding, marketing and consumer research, have been neglected. In this research, we apply a type of sensory analysis, based on several statistical techniques used to investigate the key features of ten different brands of Colombian coffee. A panel composed of 32 judges investigated nine different attributes related to flavour, fragrance, sweetness and acidity, among others. The last section presents the conclusions reached regarding customer preference and brands profiles.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne (https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03728)
citeturn155academia10 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4.6 years ago; 
Title: Evaluacion de un producto a base de aceite esencial de oregano sobre la integridad intestinal, la capacidad de absorcion de nutrientes y el comportamiento productivo de pollos de carne
Authors: Diego Martinez
Date: Thu Apr  7 20:42:43 2022

Eight experiments were conducted to test an oregano-essential-oil-based product (PRO) on performance, gut health, and nutrient absorption capacity in broilers. The first three, up to 14d and without specific challenges, tested the effects on intestinal histology, skeletal integrity, and growth. Other two experiments, up to 28d birds were challenged to induce feed passage syndrome (STR) and test the effect on the antioxidant status and performance, contrasting later the results under a natural challenge in commercial conditions. Finally, in two other experiments, up to 21 d, birds challenged with coccidia were tested to determine the effects on coccidiosis, nutrient digestibility, and feed efficiency (FCR). Corn-soybean-fish meal diets were used. Under healthy conditions, PRO effects were observed on intestinal villus height and surface area, mucosa density and structure, villus to crypt ratio, goblet cells density, mucus production, body weight gain, and FCR (P<0.04), and carcass yield and bone density (P<0.08). Birds affected by STR showed effects (P<0.05) on superoxide dismutase activity, bodyweight gain, FCRE, non-normal feces frequency, bursal diameter, and dysbacteriosis. Birds affected by coccidia showed effects on cocci-positive ratio, cocci microscopic score, oocysts count, bursal diameter, body weight gain, FCR, apparent digestibility of dry matter and crude protein, protein and energy efficiencies (P<0.01), and nitrogen apparent retention (P<0.07). Results showed PRO added value to the diet favoring feed efficiency and performance.
